newsitem.title: FRANCE: Asia/Pacific to lead $1 trillion electronics market.
newsitem.headline: Asia/Pacific to lead $1 trillion electronics market.

text.p: World electronics production will easily breach $1.2 billion by the year 2000, according to a study by high technology consultant Dataquest.

Production of personal computers, the semiconductor industry and communications and multimedia devices will be worth $1.2 trillion in 2000, compared with $750 billion last year, and will reach $2.2 trillion by 2010, Dataquest analyst Jim Eastlake told a conference in Cannes.

"Our research shows a continuing explosion in worldwide personal computer sales. This year sales will jump 20 percent to just over 70 million and we expect each of the next three years to grow around 18 percent to hit just under 120 million in 1999," Eastlake said.
Although powerful growth by most industry standards, it represents a slight slowing from 1994's 23 percent and 1995's 24 percent.
According to Dataquest, Intel Corp. is still the No. 1 one producer of semiconductors, closely followed by the Japanese firms NEC, Toshiba, and Hitachi.

Dataquest forecast that the semiconductor business alone will reach $310 billion by 2000 and $700 billion by 2005. In 1995 and 1996 the figure was stuck at around $150 billion, because of a slowing of U.S. business investment.

Asia/Pacific companies from countries other than Japan, like South Korea and Singapore, will edge ahead of North America in 1999 to account for just over 30 percent of the world's market by 2000, he said.
North America's share will dip to just under 30 percent, with Europe and Japan each with slightly over 20 percent, Dataquest said.
